Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Product Sales is a team of deep functional and technical specialists who both lead and advise on deals for the most strategically important products in Stripe’s portfolio. 

Stripe is expanding its Link Product Sales team, and this role is focused exclusively on bank payments. As an Account Executive, you will help businesses give their customers a fast, trusted way to pay from a bank account using Stripe’s full stack of payments solutions while accelerating the growth of the Link network. Few roles offer such a direct opportunity to shape and grow one of Stripe’s top company priorities. 

What you’ll do

As a founding Account Executive for Bank Payments, you will play a central role in shaping and executing Stripe’s go-to-market strategy for this growing product area. You will partner closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and other GTM teams to build deep product and industry expertise, lead complex deals, and guide in-depth conversations with existing and prospective customers. You will bring customer and market insights back to Stripe, helping influence both the product roadmap and how we take bank payments to market.

Bank payments and account connectivity are also an important part of Link’s broader vision for the future of commerce. Where the opportunity intersects with adjacent Link priorities—such as agentic commerce—you will help explore emerging customer use cases and shape how Stripe brings new experiences to market. This gives you the opportunity to build a focused bank payments business while contributing to some of Stripe’s most forward-looking initiatives.

You are an adept sales professional who can lead business and technical conversations at every level of an organization. You know how to establish value in competitive situations and are energized by products that require deep industry expertise and technical fluency. You are equally comfortable working with customers and internal partners, eager to develop and share expertise, and motivated by the opportunity to build in a fast-moving environment. You are an entrepreneurial self-starter, an exceptional communicator, and an analytical thinker with a record of top performance and making the teams around you better.

Responsibilities

  • Drive revenue, adoption, and new customer acquisition for Stripe’s bank-payments portfolio across enterprise and platform customers
  • Create a strategic territory plan, lead outreach efforts, and partner with core account teams to develop a robust, qualified bank payments pipeline
  • Develop relationships with executive stakeholders and lead business and technical discussions with existing and prospective customers
  • Advise customers on bank payment use cases and tradeoffs, including conversion, account verification, returns, fraud risk, settlement experience, and costs
  • Deeply understand Stripe’s bank payments products and competitors, serving as an internal and customer-facing expert on the portfolio and market
  • Identify early-adopter customers and turn successful engagements into repeatable discovery, positioning, and deal-execution playbooks
  • Engage with Product and Engineering teams to synthesize customer, win/loss, and competitive feedback that informs Stripe’s product roadmap
  • Contribute to go-to-market playbooks alongside Product, Marketing, Sales, and Technical Services stakeholders
  • Work collaboratively across Stripe to shape bank-payment products and solutions that meet customer needs

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Requirements

  • 10+ years of customer facing experience at a leading technology or payments company and a track record of top performance
  • Experience building trusted advisor relationships with senior business leaders
  • Proven ability to build strong collaborative working relationships with cross-functional business partners
  • Self-starter capable of operating independently to drive meaningful business results
  • Enthusiastic “roll up your sleeves” mentality
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Ability to understand complex technical requirements and craft solutions across multiple stakeholders
  • Proven experience to lead complex negotiations involving bespoke commercial agreements
  • Thrives in a fast-paced environment and changing requirements
  • True team player - always
  • Humor is very welcomed

Preferred Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience selling enterprise payments or technology solutions, ideally in bank payments, open banking, account verification, payment risk, or money movement
  • Strong understanding of ACH, Pay by Bank, and open banking payment flows, including how conversion, verification, returns, fraud risk, payment guarantees, settlement, and customer experience intersect
  • Experience launching or scaling a new payments product or category, with a track record of translating early customer wins and market feedback into repeatable go-to-market programs

About Bitdeer:

Bitdeer is a world-leading technology company for Bitcoin mining and AI cloud.

Bitdeer is committed to providing comprehensive Bitcoin mining solutions for its customers. Apart from designing industry-leading ASIC chips and manufacturing mining rigs, the Group handles complex processes involved in computing across the value chain. This includes equipment procurement, transport logistics, datacenter design and construction, equipment management, and network and facility operations. Bitdeer also offers advanced cloud capabilities to customers with a high demand for artificial intelligence.

Headquartered in Singapore, Bitdeer operates globally with a diversified 3 GW energy portfolio, and deploys Bitcoin mining and HPC datacenters in the United States, Bhutan, Norway, Canada, Malaysia, and Ethiopia.

About the role

We are seeking an Inference Performance Engineer to make Bitdeer AI's MaaS platform's benchmarks, capacity plans, and cost projections trustworthy proxies for what customers actually run in production. Today, load tests are built on prompt and output length assumptions and concurrency patterns that were reasonable a quarter ago but no longer match the traffic mix flowing through chat, completion, and embedding endpoints — the result is GPU fleets sized against a workload that doesn't exist, cost-per-token figures that surprise finance at quarter close, and latency percentile dashboards that different teams calculate differently and therefore don't trust. This role exists to close that gap: characterizing real production traffic shapes, keeping benchmarking harnesses honest against that reality, and turning the results into capacity and unit-economics numbers the business can plan around with confidence. The person who thrives here is a rigorous, data-first systems thinker who is equally comfortable pulling apart a token-length histogram, arguing with a serving-stack engineer about tail latency, and explaining a GPU-hour cost model to finance — someone who treats every metric definition as a contract other teams will build on, not a throwaway number.

What you will be responsible for:

  • Traffic and Workload Characterization: Continuously profile real production request streams across chat, completions, embeddings, and fine-tuning endpoints to build and maintain statistical models of prompt length, output length, concurrency, and burstiness by model and customer segment. Surface how these distributions shift over time and by tenant so that benchmarking, capacity, and pricing decisions are grounded in what the platform actually serves rather than stale assumptions. Package these findings into reusable traffic profiles other teams can pull from directly.
  • Harness-to-Production Fidelity: Own the validation loop between internal load-testing and benchmarking harnesses and live production behavior, auditing synthetic workload generators against the traffic profiles you maintain and flagging drift before it corrupts a capacity or optimization decision. Work with the inference serving team to update harness configurations, request mixes, and concurrency patterns whenever production shifts. Treat every benchmark result as suspect until it has been reconciled against real telemetry.
  • Capacity Planning and Unit Economics: Translate workload characterization and GPU utilization data into capacity forecasts and cost-per-token or cost-per-request models that inform fleet sizing, reservation versus on-demand mix, and pricing strategy for the MaaS product. Partner with infrastructure and finance teams to reconcile modeled costs against actual cloud and hardware spend, and maintain the analytical models that answer how many GPUs are needed and what they will cost with defensible numbers rather than gut calls.
  • Metric Definition Ownership: Define and maintain the canonical definitions for latency percentiles (time-to-first-token, inter-token latency, end-to-end), throughput, and utilization metrics used across engineering, product, and leadership dashboards, resolving disagreements between teams that compute the same-sounding metric differently. Document instrumentation requirements, aggregation windows, and edge-case handling so metric definitions stay stable as the platform and model catalog evolve, and audit dashboards for silent drift from the documented standard.
  • Cross-Team Performance Reporting: Build and maintain the dashboards, reports, and postmortem inputs that give engineering, product, and leadership a shared, trustworthy view of inference performance and cost trends, translating raw telemetry into decision-ready summaries. Act as the go-to reviewer whenever a performance or cost claim needs sanity-checking before it reaches a roadmap, pricing, or capacity decision, and coach other teams on correctly interpreting percentile and cost metrics.

How you will stand out:

  • Bring 5+ years of experience in performance engineering, capacity planning, or applied ML systems work on large-scale, GPU-backed or otherwise latency-sensitive distributed services, with at least part of that time spent directly on LLM or ML inference workloads.
  • Demonstrate hands-on experience characterizing production traffic statistically — building distributions of request rate, prompt and output token length, concurrency, and burstiness — using tools such as Python/pandas, SQL, Spark, or a comparable data-analysis stack.
  • Show working knowledge of modern LLM inference internals, including continuous batching, KV-cache management, and prefill/decode scheduling, and familiarity with serving frameworks such as vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, SGLang, or Triton Inference Server, sufficient to judge whether a benchmarking harness reflects reality.
  • Have experience designing, running, or auditing load-testing and benchmarking tooling (e.g., k6, Locust, custom load generators, or MLPerf-style suites) and reconciling their output against live production telemetry rather than treating benchmark numbers as ground truth.
  • Be comfortable partnering with finance/FinOps and infrastructure teams on GPU utilization and cost-per-token or cost-per-request modeling, including reasoning about on-demand, reserved, and spot capacity trade-offs.
  • Bring fluency with observability stacks such as Prometheus, Grafana, and distributed tracing tools, and a track record of defining metrics (latency percentiles, throughput, time-to-first-token) that hold up as the single source of truth across multiple teams.

What you will experience working with us:

  • A culture that values authenticity and diversity of thoughts and backgrounds;
  • An inclusive and respectable environment with open workspaces and exciting start-up spirit;
  • Fast-growing company with the chance to network with industrial pioneers and enthusiasts;

About the role

NeoCloud runs Infermesh, our managed Inference / Model-as-a-Service platform: customers call model endpoints over a public API and pay per token. For a service like this, reliability is the product — a failed request is not an internal incident, it is a customer-visible SLA breach. In this role you own the reliability of the inference serving path end to end: public API gateway, inference router, request scheduler and queue, prefill/decode and KV cache, inference engines, and the GPU model replicas behind them — plus the control plane and shared dependencies they rely on. Your mandate is to aim a 99.95% SLA, by closing the architecture, automation, and operational gaps that stand in the way. You are the SRE who stands between a fleet of H200/B300/GB300/VR NVL72 serving nodes and the customer's experience of a simple, dependable model endpoint.

What you will be responsible for:

  • End-to-end availability of customer inference endpoints — API availability, request success rate, TTFT/TPOT latency, and the published SLA.
  • The serving path: API gateway, inference router, health-based routing, request scheduler, queueing and admission control, prefill/decode serving, and the KV cache service.
  • Inference runtime operations: engine health (vLLM / SGLang / TensorRT-LLM class runtimes), model load and readiness validation, model revision rollout and rollback.
  • Model replica topology and failure isolation: tensor-parallel group containment, GPU / NVLink / NCCL fault isolation, replica anti-affinity across nodes, racks, and failure domains.
  • Multi-cluster serving across MY / SG / JP: cross-cluster traffic steering, tested cluster failover, and regional recovery or evacuation scope.
  • GPU serving fleet health (H200 / B300 / GB300 / VR NVL72 bare metal): DCGM / Xid / ECC monitoring, automated drain and cordon, replica replacement with no sustained customer impact.
  • The Kubernetes platform beneath the serving path: HA control plane, etcd, CNI, CoreDNS, public / management / east-west edge tiers, and egress NAT.
  • Shared control-plane dependencies: PostgreSQL (including Temporal), Redis, Vault secrets and certificates, object storage and model registry, ClickHouse — HA, tested failover, and decoupling live serving from control-plane outages.
  • Capacity and saturation engineering: GPU utilization, KV cache occupancy, queue depth and concurrency; N+1 headroom, admission control, load shedding, and graceful degradation instead of collapse.
  • The SLI/SLO/SLA system: define and instrument the SLIs, publish the SLOs, run error budgets and burn-rate alerting, and produce customer-facing SLA reporting.
  • Observability stack — VictoriaMetrics, VictoriaLogs, Tempo, Pyroscope, Grafana, ClickHouse — plus external synthetic inference probes that exercise the real customer API path.
  • Incident management: severity model, incident commander rotation, primary / secondary / cross-team / vendor escalation, status-page and customer communication, and postmortems with tracked actions.
  • Change safety: staged and canary rollout for application, model, and configuration changes; automatic rollback on regression; production change review and release risk classification.
  • Resilience validation: recurring failover drills, DR tests, game days and fault injection, and backup restore verification — with measured RTO as the evidence.

Reliability ownership

  • You are accountable for the customer's reliability experience — when an endpoint degrades, a replica dies, or a router loses a backend, you own detection, remediation, and the communication loop.
  • Drive the platform from to 99.95%, using the SLA gap assessment — architecture, operations, and failure-mode matrices — as your roadmap.
  • Own the failure-mode and resilience matrix: every Critical and High failure mode gets a detection signal, a mitigation path, a target RTO, and a drill that proves it.
  • Define and publish customer-facing SLOs and SLAs, and drive error-budget-based prioritization between feature work and reliability work.
  • Partner with support and customer success to close the loop from customer-reported issues to systemic fixes, and build tenant-visible status, usage, and quota observability that reduces support load.

How we build software is changing. Designers are building tools and agents, prototyping in code, and shipping directly into the product. More people can create software than ever before. That makes design judgment more important, not less.

We’re looking for a Design Systems Lead to build that judgment into the foundations of Ramp.

This is not just about maintaining a component library. It’s about making it possible for designers, engineers, and agents to build experiences that look, feel, and work like Ramp—without a designer driving every decision or the design systems team reviewing every change.

You’re a designer first, with the technical depth to guide architecture and get into the code. You have exceptional taste and strong opinions about typography, hierarchy, interaction, and motion. Just as importantly, you know how to turn that judgment into patterns, tools, and guidance that make everyone else’s work better.

You’re deeply curious about AI and already using it to change how you work. You build, experiment, inspect the results, and push past the demo. You can imagine a different way of building software—and lead a team toward it.

This role is for you if you’re excited by:

  • Making great design reproducible. Raise the quality of Ramp’s product and encode what makes it good, so people and agents can produce coherent, usable experiences by default. The system should make excellent work easier, not make every experience look the same.

  • Reimagining what a design system can be. Build beyond components and tokens into composition, interaction patterns, agent guidance, and evaluations. Connect exploration and production so the fastest way to build is also a path to great quality.

  • Leading a team that multiplies everyone else’s impact. Create clear direction, ambitious goals, and a caring yet demanding environment. Inspire curiosity, develop people, and stay close enough to the work to help make it exceptional.

The opportunity is to raise the floor for everyone building at Ramp, while giving designers more room to make the most important experiences extraordinary.

What You'll Do

  • Elevate Ramp’s visual and interaction design. Raise the bar for typography, hierarchy, density, motion, responsive behavior, accessibility, and the states beyond the happy path.

  • Make design judgment usable by people and agents. Translate principles into reusable patterns, reference experiences, composition rules, and guidance that produce better work without you in the room.

  • Guide technical architecture with engineering. Shape everything from components and tokens to how agents discover guidance, compose interfaces, and check their work. Make sound tradeoffs between flexibility, coherence, performance, and ease of use.

  • Stay hands-on. Build prototypes, work in code, and get into implementation details to test ideas, unblock the team, and understand where the system breaks down.

  • Define and measure quality. Build repeatable evaluations grounded in real tasks. Measure whether builders can ship better work faster, with less rework—not just whether they use the tools.

  • Improve the path from idea to shipped experience. Partner with engineering and AI teams on workflows that support fast exploration, useful iteration, and appropriate production safeguards.

What You Need

You own the mechanics that make the TPRM program run day to day.   • Issues: maintaining the TPRM issues log from identification through remediation and closure.

  • Reverse Due Diligence: supporting due diligence requests that come from partners and counterparties assessing Augustus.

 

Your first 90 days

Founded in 2012 by 3 expert hackers with no investment capital, Trail of Bits is the premier place for security experts to boldly advance security and address technology's newest and most challenging risks. Cybersecurity preparedness is a moving target. Companies like ours are the tip of the spear in the fight against attackers. Our research-based and custom-engineering approach ensures that our client's capabilities are at the forefront of what's available. For companies and technologies that live and die by their security, a proactive, tailored approach is required to keep one step ahead of attackers.

Democratizing security information is essential. As part of our business, we provide ongoing informational support through blogs, whitepapers, newsletters, meetups, and open-source tools. The more the community understands security, the more they'll understand why a company like ours is so unique and valuable.

The Role

Trail of Bits seeks a Security Engineer I for our Application Security practice. You will contribute to security assessments of client software, partner with more experienced engineers, identify vulnerabilities across the application and system levels, and own clearly scoped pieces of client engagements. You will drive your own vulnerability analysis, develop tools alongside the team, and help clients understand and fix the issues you find.

This role bridges vulnerability research and applied security. Your work will be hands-on: analyzing complex code, building custom tooling, conducting threat modeling, and owning your findings through client delivery. It is distinct from roles centered on security operations, SOC work, GRC, compliance, policy, audit, or general security administration. Candidates from broader or adjacent security backgrounds should be prepared to talk through relevant hands-on, code-level security work they have personally completed.

Security Engineer I is an early-career role, but it is not a training role for someone new to software or security. Relevant experience may come from professional work, internships, advanced coursework, independent research, open-source contributions, CTFs, or substantial personal or academic projects. Regardless of where you gained the experience, you should be able to talk through code-level security work you performed, how you approached the problem, and the conclusions you reached. You will receive direction and review from a project lead while independently completing well-scoped technical work.

  • Custom Security Tooling: Design and build security-testing tools and automation for vulnerability detection and deeper analysis.
  • Architecture and Threat Modeling: Review software architectures, identify attack surfaces, data flows, trust and privilege boundaries, and recommend concrete mitigations.
  • Client Communication: Translate technical findings into clear, actionable recommendations for engineering teams and explain the evidence behind your conclusions.
  • Research and Innovation: Contribute to security research, open-source tools, internal knowledge sharing, and technical documentation.

What You'll Bring

The following are requirements for this role:

  • At least 1 year of combined relevant experience in application security, vulnerability research, security-focused software engineering, or a closely related area. This experience may come from employment, internships, advanced coursework, independent research, open-source contributions, CTFs, or substantial personal or academic projects.
  • Demonstrable vulnerability-discovery capability. You can talk through a vulnerability or security weakness you personally found or validated, including how you identified it, established its impact, and reached your conclusion. Evidence may come from professional work, coursework, projects, CTFs, CVEs, bug bounties, responsible disclosure, open source, or comparable research.
  • Strong code-analysis skills. You can read unfamiliar code, trace execution and data flow, identify logic or implementation flaws, and distinguish a tool signal from a validated vulnerability.
  • Hands-on coding proficiency in at least two relevant languages, such as Rust, Go, C, C++, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, or similar languages used in security analysis and tool development.
  • Working knowledge of memory-corruption vulnerabilities and common mitigations, such as buffer overflows, use-after-free, stack cookies, ASLR, NX/DEP, CFI, or MTE, including the ability to reason about exploit primitives at an appropriate early-career level.
  • Familiarity with operating-system concepts, IPC, privilege boundaries, and the ways applications interact with system internals.
  • Ability to independently investigate a well-scoped problem, debug issues, document evidence, ask focused questions when blocked, and deliver work with review from a project lead.

You will help partners understand and adopt new Stripe primitives, product capabilities, and integration opportunities. You will turn partner feedback and market context into clear priorities, coordinate cross-functional work, and ensure that partner programs are effective, measurable, and easy to engage with.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys building scalable programs, bringing structure to ambiguous work, and enabling many partners to succeed.

Responsibilities

  • Manage a broad portfolio of ecosystem partners through scalable programs, tiers, communications, and operating mechanisms.
  • Help design, launch, and operate partner programs that provide clear value to partners and advance Stripe’s ecosystem and product priorities.
  • Create and maintain partner tiering, engagement models, program criteria, and lifecycle motions that make it easier to prioritize support and scale partner impact.
  • Drive adoption of new Stripe primitives, product capabilities, and partner-facing initiatives across the ecosystem. Develop partner enablement plans and track adoption, engagement, and delivery against defined KPIs.
  • Work closely with Partner Engineering to surface partner integration needs, identify recurring technical or product friction, coordinate enablement, and improve the partner integration experience.
  • Work closely with Product Marketing to develop partner messaging, launches, education, and campaigns that help partners understand Stripe’s value proposition and take action.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Go-to-Market, Operations, PE&O, RPS, and other stakeholders to translate partner insights into clear workstreams, resolve blockers, and execute effectively.

  • Develop a strong understanding of the ecosystem, partner objectives and constraints, Stripe’s product capabilities, and relevant market developments. Share material insights and recommendations with internal stakeholders.
  • Build productive relationships across Stripe and with partners, communicate clearly, and help align stakeholders with competing priorities around shared outcomes.
  • Contribute to an inclusive, high-performing team culture and apply Stripe’s operating principles in day-to-day work.

You are a thoughtful, execution-oriented partnerships professional who is energized by operating at scale. You enjoy building programs, defining tiers and operating models, and improving the systems that enable many partners to succeed. You can build context quickly, turn it into clear plans, and collaborate well across functions with different goals and perspectives.

  • Interest in Stripe’s products, our users, and the ecosystem in which we operate.

  • Experience with ecosystem, platform, technology, payments, financial-services, or SaaS partnerships.
  • Experience driving adoption of new product capabilities, integrations, or platform primitives through partner enablement, education, or go-to-market programs.
  • Experience working closely with partner-facing engineering, product, or product-marketing teams.
  • Familiarity with partner integrations, commercial agreements, partner operations, or risk and compliance considerations in a regulated or complex environment.
